problems.quote: (a) ... rounds keep closing on or below their reported targets, with dearer debt and no freeze ... (b) A visible freeze: two or more large AI listings or rounds are pulled or cut, including a delay at OpenAI or Anthropic ... (c) A renewed rush: rounds close above their targets, valuations rise
problems.problem: The text claims the scenarios 'cover every outcome' and 'exclude each other', but they do not yet. (a) and (c) overlap when some rounds close above target and others below. A quarter in which large rounds neither close nor are pulled fits none of the three. It is unclear whether Firmus counts toward 'two or more', although Confirms for (b) says 'a second shelved listing', and whether a delay at OpenAI or Anthropic is required for (b) or is only an example.
problems.suggested_fix: Make (a) the remainder so coverage holds by definition: '(b) A visible freeze: two or more large AI listings or rounds, Firmus included, are pulled or cut; a delay at OpenAI or Anthropic counts as one. (c) A renewed rush: no further pull, and most large rounds that close do so above their targets at higher values. (a) The base case, everything else: money keeps flowing at a higher price ...' The probabilities can stay as they are.

problems.quote: Weakens: either of the other two scenarios.
problems.problem: This names no observable signal, unlike every other Weakens line, and rule 5.5 asks for what would weaken the forecast. As written it is circular.
problems.suggested_fix: Weakens: a second shelved listing, or a run of rounds closing above their targets.

problems.quote: it is an organised call by a group of leading mathematicians to stop working with a lab
problems.problem: 'Leading mathematicians' is not in the sources. C04-01 says only that the Association for Human Mathematics is chaired by Fields Medalist Terence Tao. My earlier suggested wording carried the same overstatement.
problems.suggested_fix: it is an organised call by a mathematicians' group chaired by Fields Medalist Terence Tao to stop working with a lab

problems.quote: Memory is getting dearer and optical parts are sold out
problems.problem: This turns one chief executive's claim about Lumentum's own parts (C08-08) into a statement about all optical parts, and it drops the hedge that the watch list below keeps. My earlier suggested wording had the same flaw.
problems.suggested_fix: Memory is getting dearer and a major optical supplier says it is sold out, so building costs more as borrowing does.

problems.where: S3 '3. Safety, security and law', paragraph 1, Inference (fix 6)
problems.quote: the card industry's rule for AI agents is that an agent may look but a person must say yes
problems.problem: The paragraph's own Fact and C12-06 say the PCI text is advisory guidance and that existing requirements take precedence, so 'rule' overstates it. 'May look' is also not in the guidance, which recommends human approval for any action involving readable card data.
problems.suggested_fix: Inference: the card industry's advice for AI agents is that a person must approve any action they take on readable card details; Seoul's response so far is a security self-assessment, not an AI rule.

problems.where: S1 '1. What AI can do now', paragraph 0, Inference (fix 2)
problems.quote: Google's first judgement will come from a closed group whose findings the public cannot check
problems.problem: This is a clarity problem only. 'Google's first judgement' reads as a judgement made by Google, not the first verdict on Google's model.
problems.suggested_fix: the first verdict on Google's model will come from a closed group whose findings the public cannot check

problems.where: D. Key unknowns, last Missing data (fix 18)

problems.quote: At least one more maker of AI chips or components announces a price rise tied to the memory shortage by early January.
problems.problem: 'One more ... announces' implies that the Huawei and Cambricon rises were announced. Per C08-10 they come from three unnamed people, and the companies did not comment.
problems.suggested_fix: At least one maker of AI chips or components publicly announces a price rise tied to the memory shortage by early January.
